subtitle.en: Making some simple changes to the lister panel code so that its display could show a hierarchy.
subtitle.zh: 对 Lister Panel 的代码做几处小改动，让它的显示支持层级结构。

translator.note: 归档源码里有多行代码被拆出了 cpp 代码块（已并回各自的代码块），另有一段正文被误放进 cpp 代码块（已按正文段落译出）；代码一律保留英文原样，原文没有配图。

blocks.en: The problem with the internet is that everyone thinks they're an expert.  That would be fine, if everyone actually was an expert, but the truth is that only I am an expert, so it's just frustrating.
blocks.zh: 互联网的问题在于，每个人都觉得自己是专家。如果每个人真的是专家，那倒也没什么；可惜事实是只有我是专家，所以这就很让人烦躁。

blocks.en: To give a simple example, someone wrote in to say that they were "promised" references to the [Chronicles of Narnia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chronicles_of_Narnia) in Part 14 of this series, and that Part 15 failed to deliver on that "promise".  Nothing could be further from the truth.  This is a perfect example of someone thinking they know what they're talking about when they clearly don't.
blocks.zh: 举个简单的例子：有人写信来说，本系列第 14 篇「承诺过」要提到 [Chronicles of Narnia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chronicles_of_Narnia)（《纳尼亚传奇》），而第 15 篇没有兑现那个「承诺」。这离事实简直不能再远了。这就是「明明完全不懂，却以为自己很懂」的绝佳范例。

blocks.en: If you go back and read Part 15, you will plainly see that the entire article is all one giant Chronicles of Narnia reference, but because I am actually an expert on the series (unlike the erroneous commenter), I chose to reference something subtle that only other experts would understand.  As devotees of the Chronicles know, one of the primary villains in the later books is the snail-mage Shellius Grubb, who often uses his magical powers to entrap the minds of his enemies into long daydreams about things that are completely unrelated to Narnia.  This was precisely how I constructed Part 15 of Witness Wednesday, and if you were a true fan of the Narnia books  —  not those horrific movie adaptations  —  you would have seen this immediately.
blocks.zh: 如果你回头去读第 15 篇，你会清楚地看到：整篇文章就是一整套巨大的《纳尼亚传奇》梗；只不过因为我才是这个系列的真专家（不像那位搞错的评论者），我选择的是一种含蓄的致敬，只有别的专家才看得懂。读过这套书的人都知道，后面几部里的主要反派之一是蜗牛法师 Shellius Grubb，他常施展法力，把敌人的心智困在漫长的白日梦里，去神游那些和 Narnia 毫无关系的东西。第 15 篇的 Witness Wednesday 正是这么构造出来的；如果你是纳尼亚原著（而不是那些糟糕的电影改编）的真粉丝，你一眼就能看出来。

blocks.en: But in addition to being an expert, I am also a professional, so I do not let amateur comments like this deter me from the important task of making subtle long-form references to outdated [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II) allegories.  So without further ado, here is one of the many famous speeches [Prince Caspian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chronicles_of_Narnia:_Prince_Caspian) used to address his people during the myriad national holidays celebrated in Narnia:
blocks.zh: 但除了是专家，我还是个专业人士，所以这种业余的评论丝毫不能阻止我去做那件重要的事：对着过时的 [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)（第二次世界大战）寓言做含蓄的长篇致敬。那么闲话少说，下面是 [Prince Caspian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chronicles_of_Narnia:_Prince_Caspian)（凯斯宾王子）在 Narnia 名目繁多的国定假日里向子民发表的众多著名演讲之一：

blocks.en: "Ladies and gentlemen of Narnia, loyal subjects, let me tell you about the time when the lion was being a real dick and he locked me inside the wardrobe, and I had to escape by adding hierarchical group display to [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/) editor's Lister Panel…"
blocks.zh: 「Narnia 的女士们先生们，忠诚的臣民们，让我给你们讲讲那一次，那头狮子实在混蛋得可以，把我锁在衣柜里，而我最后是靠给 [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/) 编辑器的 Lister Panel 加上分层 group 显示，才逃出来的……」
缩进式列表
blocks.en: Indented Listings

The original Lister Panel didn't actually display groups of things at all.  It was strictly a flat, linear list of entities.  So when I updated the Lister Panel to have scrolling displays and filtering options and other fancinesses, it seemed like a good time to add basic hierarchical listing support to bring it more in line with what artists use in packages like [3DSMAX](http://www.autodesk.com/products/autodesk-3ds-max/overview) and [Maya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autodesk_Maya).  [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/)'s entity model already included hierarchically nested groups, there just wasn't any way to ever see them in a standard "tree view"-style list.
blocks.zh: 最初的 Lister Panel 其实根本不显示成组的东西。它严格来说就是一份平铺的、线性的实体列表。所以当我给 Lister Panel 加上可滚动显示、过滤选项和其他花哨功能时，感觉正是加上基本的分层列表支持的好时机，好让它更接近美术们在 [3DSMAX](http://www.autodesk.com/products/autodesk-3ds-max/overview) 和 [Maya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autodesk_Maya) 这类软件里用的那套东西。《The Witness》的实体模型本来就已经有可以层级嵌套的 group 了，只是一直没有任何办法在一个标准的「树形视图」式列表里看到它们。

blocks.en: To show items in a tree view, obviously you have to traverse them depth-first, because for each item at a certain level of the tree, you don't list the next item at its level until you've listed all of its "children", and all of its children's children, and so on.  This is the classic case for a simple recursive function, assuming you know that the depth of the tree and the size of the stack aren't onerous:
blocks.zh: 要让条目以树形视图显示，显然得按深度优先的方式遍历它们，因为对树上某一层的每个条目来说，你得先把它的所有「子节点」、以及子节点的子节点等等都列出来，才能去列它同层的下一个条目。假设你清楚树的深度和栈的大小都不成问题，这就是简单递归函数的经典场景：

blocks.en: Of course, it is always worth taking a moment to think about the assumptions.  Every time you call a function, all of its locals get pushed onto the program's stack.  So a recursive call acts like a multiplier on the stack space required to execute the function.  If the stack space required for the function is 1k, and the maximum depth of recursion if 100, then you can ballpark 100k of stack space, which probably isn't an issue on any modern platform.  On the otherhand, if the function did something like this:
blocks.zh: 当然，花点时间想想这些假设总是值得的。每次调用一个函数，它的所有局部变量都会被压进程序的栈里。因此，递归调用相当于给执行这个函数所需的栈空间乘了一个倍数。如果这个函数需要的栈空间是 1k，而递归的最大深度是 100，那你大概可以估出 100k 的栈空间——在任何现代平台上这大概都不成问题。反过来说，如果这个函数干的是这种事：

blocks.en: Now you have a problem.  Each invocation of the function requires over 64k of stack space, so a recursion depth of 100 now requires over 6 megabytes of stack space just for the buffer variable alone.  This can get out of hand quickly:
blocks.zh: 现在你有麻烦了。函数的每一次调用都需要超过 64k 的栈空间，那么深度为 100 的递归光是那个 buffer 变量就要占掉 6 兆字节以上的栈空间。这种事很快就会失控：

blocks.en: Now we're up to over 65536*1024 = 64 megabytes of stack space *per invocation*, or over 6 gigabytes for a 100-deep recursion.  That's a (hopefully) absurd example, but serves to illustrate the point that the multipliers all cascade, and you should always be aware of how otherwise harmless counts can quickly combine to yield unwieldy combinations.
blocks.zh: 现在我们到了每次调用超过 65536*1024 = 64 兆字节栈空间的地步，也就是深度 100 的递归要 6 吉字节以上。这个例子（但愿）荒谬得很，但它说明了一点：这些倍数会层层叠加，你应该时刻意识到，本来无害的几个数字一凑，很快就会组合出难以收拾的结果。

blocks.en: And, as an aside, it's worth noting that sometimes your code can end up being used in more extreme circumstances than what you consider appropriate.  In The Witness, there was a piece of code I wrote that used a recursive function to traverse some collision data.  I did the mental check at the time and knew that it would be safe for all the cases that could happen in the shipping product.  But I did not consider what might happen when it was used in other scenarios.  And it just so happened that when that code was called in debug mode, where you can fly around and do a bunch of things you cannot do in the release build, the amount of traversal it would have to do could grow considerably and the stack could overflow.  The stack, even on PC, is often set to a smaller size than you would think.  I ended up having to change the code from recursion to a loop with explicit storage.  So really, it can often be better to be safe than sorry with this kind of thing.
blocks.zh: 另外顺便说一句：有时候你的代码会被用在比你认为合适的场景更极端的环境里。在《The Witness》里就有我写的一段代码，用递归函数去遍历一些碰撞数据。我当时在脑子里核对过，知道对正式发售的产品里可能出现的所有情况它都是安全的。但我没考虑它在别的场景下被调用会怎样。结果恰好就是：当那段代码在调试模式下被调用时——调试模式下你可以到处飞、干一堆在正式版里干不了的事——它要遍历的量可能急剧增长，栈就可能溢出。栈这个东西，即便在 PC 上，往往也被设得比你想象的更小。我最后只好把代码从递归改成了带显式存储的循环。所以在这类事情上，「宁可多一分小心」往往真的比「事后后悔」好。

blocks.en: For the hierarchical entity listing, I was confident that recursion was OK, primarily because the depth of recursion is guaranteed to be very low.  Artists generally cannot deal with groups that are nested inside other groups hundreds of times deep, so the maximum nesting level tends to be in the 10s at the very most, nowhere near the 100s, and the stack space per invocation in this case was negligible.
blocks.zh: 至于分层实体列表，我很确信用递归没问题，主要是因为递归深度保证会非常浅。美术一般没法应付嵌套几百层深的 group，所以最大嵌套层级顶多也就几十层，离上百层差得远，而且在这次的情形里，每次调用的栈空间开销微不足道。
保存展开状态
blocks.en: Storing the Expansion State

I knew the first step to making the hierarchical entity listing actually behave like a normal tree view was to add conditional expansion of the children, since the only thing that really makes tree views more usable than straight lists is their convenient collapsibility.  So I needed to write something like this:
blocks.zh: 我知道，要让分层实体列表真正像普通树形视图那样工作，第一步是给子节点加上有条件的展开，因为树形视图比平铺列表真正好用的地方就在于它能方便地折叠。所以我需要写这样一段代码：

blocks.en: But the problem is, whether or not a group entity is expanded in the Lister Panel isn't really something that should be stored on the entity itself.  First, it would prevent ever having more than one Lister Panel, because the group would expand and collapse in all the lists at once if there was just one notion of "expanded" state.  Second, as a policy, it invites disaster by suggesting that everyone who ever needs to do anything with entities should just dump that data into the entity itself, which bloats the class and takes up a lot of space unnecessarily, not to mention making it very hard to read and understand what an entity class contains.
blocks.zh: 但问题在于，「某个 group 实体在 Lister Panel 里是否展开」这件事，其实并不该存在实体自己身上。第一，这样一来就永远不可能有第二个 Lister Panel 了，因为如果「展开」状态只有一份，那么这个 group 会在所有列表里同时展开和折叠。第二，作为一种方针，它是在招灾：它在暗示每个要拿实体做事的人都可以把数据往实体里一塞了事，这会让类变得臃肿、白白占掉大量空间，更别提还会让人极难读懂一个实体类里到底装了什么。

blocks.en: So I chose the more localized approach of having the Lister Panel store the set of entities that were expanded in its listing:
blocks.zh: 所以我选了更局部的做法：让 Lister Panel 自己保存「在它的列表里处于展开状态的实体」这个集合：

blocks.en: When I say "set", I actually mean the logical notion of a set, and not the STL set class.  In the case of The Witness codebase, it actually has very few fundamental algorithm utilities, and so there isn't a notion of a "set".  But there is a hash table, and a hash table can obviously be used to store a set by just using the key part of the hash and ignoring the data part: if the key is found, then the entity is expanded in the Lister Panel, if it is not found, then it is collapsed.  Nice and simple.
blocks.zh: 我说「集合」时，指的是逻辑意义上的集合，不是 STL 的 set 类。《The Witness》的代码库其实几乎没有几个基础算法工具，所以并不存在「集合」这个概念。但它有哈希表，而哈希表显然可以用来存集合——只用哈希的键部分、忽略数据部分就行：键找得到，就说明该实体在 Lister Panel 里是展开的；找不到，就是折叠的。干净又简单。

blocks.en: As an aside, if you're looking at this code and wondering why the return value for expansion_button() wasn't designed to be something that could be used cleanly in this case, I can elaborate a bit on that.  First, the common case for expansion_button() is actually the case where there is just a boolean that stores the expansion state:
blocks.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你看着这段代码，心里纳闷 expansion_button() 的返回值当初为什么不设计成在这里能干净使用的形式，我可以稍微展开讲讲。首先，expansion_button() 最常见的用法其实是「只有一个布尔值来保存展开状态」的情形：

blocks.en: So the code is squeaky-clean in that case.  In the case with the hash table, different work needs to be done depending on whether expansion or collapse happened, and, more crucially, work only happens when the state changes.  In order to write this cleanly, you would have to return whether or not the state was toggled:
blocks.zh: 所以在那种情形下，代码干净得发光。而换成哈希表的情形，就要根据这次是展开还是折叠做不同的事，而且更关键的是：只有状态发生变化时才需要做事。要把它写干净，你就得返回「状态是否被切换了」：

blocks.en: Unfortunately, this makes the common case a little uglier:
blocks.zh: 可惜这么一来，最常见的那种情形就变得难看了些：

blocks.en: So I preferred the prior way.  It's conceivable that you might introduce a second function so you can have it both ways, but that seems like overkill unless you anticipate having a lot of both cases in the code, which isn't the case with [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/).
blocks.zh: 所以我更喜欢前一种写法。你当然可以再加第二个函数，好把两种方式都留给你用，但除非你预计代码里这两种情形都很多，否则这显得有点过度了——而《The Witness》并不是那种情况。
过滤
blocks.en: Filtering

I now had a Lister Panel that could list things hierarchically, but it couldn't actually perform its filtering when things were listed hierarchically, since I had not yet put in any code to call the filter.  It may seem like an easy addition of just calling the old "passes_filter" call at each step of the hierarchy, but doing filtering that way has a drawback: if you want to, you can't actually display the parent groups of things that are included in the filter unless the parent groups are also included in the filter.
blocks.zh: 现在我的 Lister Panel 能分层列出东西了，但当东西是分层列出的时候，它其实还没法做过滤，因为我还没写任何调用过滤器的代码。这看起来似乎很容易加上：只要在层级的每一步调用过去那个 passes_filter 就行。但这样过滤有个缺点：如果你愿意的话，你没法显示那些被过滤出来的东西的父级 group——除非父级 group 本身也通过了过滤。

blocks.en: In other words, say you want to see all grass entities in the world, but you want to see them in a view that shows the complete hierarchy leading up to each grass entity.  Ie., if a grass entity was inside a group, you want to see that group expanded and the grass entity inside it, but you don't want to see any other groups or any of the non-grass entities inside the group.  This is a pretty common operation to want to do, since often times you want to manipulate the groups that things are in, but the only way to find those groups is by talking about the things that are in them.  So filters are usually best written on non-groups even if you want to manipulate the groups themselves.
blocks.zh: 换句话说，假设你想看到世界里所有的草（grass）实体，但你希望这个视图把通向每个草实体的完整层级都显示出来。也就是说，如果某个草实体在一个 group 里，你希望看到那个 group 展开、草实体在它里面，但你不想看到别的 group，也不想看到那个 group 里任何不是草的实体。这是相当常见的一种需求，因为很多时候你想操作的是「东西所属的那些 group」，而要找到这些 group，唯一的线索就是它们在装着的那些东西。所以，即便你想操作的是 group 本身，过滤器通常也最好写在非 group 的东西上。

blocks.en: Filtering like this is not something that can readily be performed during a depth-first walk of the hierarchy, and even if it was, it's not clear that the code should work that way, since part of the idea behind the Lister Panel was that the rendering code wouldn't iterate over all the entities all the time, it would only iterate over the filtered entities as found by the update() function, to ensure that it could still be used if the total entity count got too large.  So what I needed to do was write a prepass that went through the filtered entities and figured out what groups should be "pulled in" by the filtered entities if the Lister Panel was set to a mode where the hierarchy was always supposed to be shown.
blocks.zh: 这样的过滤没法在层级深度优先的遍历过程中顺手完成；而且就算能，也不清楚代码是否该那样工作，因为 Lister Panel 背后的部分设计意图就是：渲染代码不要时刻遍历所有实体，而是只遍历 update() 函数找出来的、被过滤之后的实体，以保证实体总数变得很大时它依然可用。所以我需要做的，是写一趟预遍历：走一遍被过滤出来的实体，算出在 Lister Panel 被设成「总是显示层级」的模式时，这些实体应该把哪些 group「拉进来」。

blocks.en: There is a very easy way to write code like this in a structure where it is easy to ask what the "parent" of something in a hierarchy is.  It is related to (but simpler than) the "disjoint set forest" data structure, which I highly recommend reading about if it's not already in your wheelhouse of programming tools.  The idea is simple: iterate over all the entities that you want to display.  For each one, check to see if you've processed it already.  If you haven't, walk its pointer up to the root of the hierarchy, processing each entity along the way.  This ensures that you visit each entity only once, that you never visit any entity other than the filtered entities and their ancestors, and that you always visit all ancestors of the filtered entities:
blocks.zh: 在一个能方便地问出「层级里某个东西的父级是谁」的结构里，写这类代码有一个非常简单的办法。它和「不相交集合森林」（disjoint set forest）这种数据结构有关（但更简单）；如果你的编程工具箱里还没有它，我强烈建议去了解一下。思路很简单：遍历所有你想显示的实体。对每一个，先检查自己是否已经处理过。如果没处理过，就沿着它的指针一路向上走到层级的根，途中把每个实体都处理一遍。这能保证：每个实体只被访问一次；除了被过滤出来的实体及其祖先之外，别的实体一个都不会被访问；而且被过滤实体的所有祖先都一定会被访问到：

blocks.en: During this iteration, I also keep track of a "top_level" array, which stores any entity at the root of the hierarchy.  It checks the Lister Panel setting to see whether or not entities are supposed to be listed hierarchically, and if they aren't, it just adds everything so it will be listed flat.  Otherwise, it only adds things at the root.
blocks.zh: 在这次迭代中，我还维护了一个 top_level 数组，用来存层级根部的实体。它会检查 Lister Panel 的设置，看实体是否应该分层列出；如果不该，那它就把所有东西都加进去，于是列表就是平铺的。否则，它就只加根部的那些东西。

blocks.en: Now, the Lister Panel also allows you to set whether or not you wanted to "pull in" all the groups of the filtered entities, as I mentioned before.  You can see in the loop above that it only continues looking for the parent if that setting is set.  If groups aren't being pulled in, you have a situation where the loop above doesn't actually add everything to the top_level that might need to be when the Lister is set to a hierarchical display.  A secondary loop makes sure that entities whose parents aren't included in the listing get added to top_level:
blocks.zh: 另外，就像我前面提到的，Lister Panel 还允许你设置要不要把所有「被过滤实体的 group」拉进来。你可以在上面的循环里看到，只有这个设置打开时，它才会继续往上找父级。如果不拉进 group，那就会出现这么一种情况：当 Lister 被设成分层显示时，上面的循环并没有把本该放进 top_level 的所有东西都放进去。于是有第二个循环来兜底，确保那些父级没被包含进列表的实体被加进 top_level：

blocks.en: Now, this seems rather inefficient to me, because I should think you could cleverly fold this logic in to the previous loop and avoid a second iteration.  Present Me suspects that Past Me was writing this code in a hurry (which I was) and either didn't realize the loops could fold together, or more probably, didn't want to spend the extra time to do so.  I will refrain from criticizing past me for the moment, but I would definitely suggest casting a slightly disapproving look in the direction of this code.  I am casting just such a look right now, in fact.
blocks.zh: 在我看来这相当低效，因为我觉得完全可以把这段逻辑巧妙地折进前一个循环，省掉第二次迭代。现在的我怀疑，过去的我写这段代码时很赶（确实很赶），要么是没意识到这两个循环可以合并，要么——更可能——是不想多花那点时间。我暂且先不批评过去的我，但我绝对建议你朝这段代码投去一个略带不满的眼神。事实上，此时此刻我就正在投去这样的眼神。
Narnia 的好日子
blocks.en: A Great Day for Narnia

And so, fair citizens of Narnia, with the possible exception of the Lion, because we are not on speaking terms at the moment, I would like to thank you  —  on behalf of myself and the King of Narnia, whom I assume exists, but, much like Lord of the Rings, I did not read this series either so I'm not entirely sure  —  for attending this glorious Witness Wendesday event!  Return, fair subjects, to the wardrobe area next week for another invigoratingly verbose excursion into The Lister Panel.
blocks.zh: 那么，Narnia 的公民们——那头狮子可能除外，因为我们目前互不搭理——我要代表我自己、以及 Narnia 的国王（我假定他存在；不过和《魔戒》一样，这套书我也没读过，所以并不十分确定），感谢各位光临这场光荣的 Witness Wendesday 盛会！忠诚的臣民们，下周请回到衣柜那片区域，再次展开一趟提神醒脑、啰里啰嗦的 The Lister Panel 之旅。
